$comment: Handshake protocol 40 binds original parameter roots at exact opening-prefix reads. Protocol 39 adds affirmative unwritten parameter bindings for whole-slot identity, not concrete shape. Protocol 38 spells complete union premises and binds each constituent identity. Protocol 37 permits an exact anonymous local callable census only when its compiler symbol independently declares that node. Protocol 36 added localLiteralResult. Consumers still bind runtime identity and execution separately.
title: TypeFactsSchema v1 (latest semantic vocabulary)
description: Length-prefixed deterministic-CBOR request and response frames exchanged with solid-typefacts. Field names are the CBOR map keys. Optional fields are omitted, never null. Handshake protocol 35 (ADR 0051) recognizes the explicit never type as a non-object fact before distributing union constituents. An empty constituent list without that explicit flag still refuses. The same predicate governs coercion forms, primitive operand premises, and primitiveCompletion: an explicit never completion states there is no normal object-valued result, not that a result type was unavailable. Caller argument premises and exact helper echoes still bind the type and its identity; a primitive completion never substitutes for censusing the callee's calls. Handshake protocol 34 (ADR 0050) widens the `parameter` derivation to a binding the file **writes**, when every value that binding can hold is rooted at one parameter. No flow analysis is involved and none is claimed: if every value the binding can hold is the caller's, then whichever one it holds at the read is the caller's, and which branch assigned it never comes up. The sources are the declaration's own initializer and the right-hand side of every plain assignment to it; a reference to the binding itself is admitted co-inductively, which is the chain rule applied to `a.b.c` written as a loop; and a declaration with no initializer contributes no source, because the value is then `undefined` and a member read of it throws before any lookup. A compound assignment, an update expression, a destructuring target and a `for…of`/`for…in` head each refuse the whole binding rather than being skipped, and sources rooted at two different slots refuse because the receipt names one. Handshake protocol 33 (ADR 0049) lets a `callArgumentPremise` cover the argument slots a call does **not** write as well as those it does: such a parameter receives `undefined` at run time, a primitive, which is a stronger premise than the `any` an unannotated parameter would otherwise carry. It is a semantic fact rather than a type one — the call has fewer arguments than the callee has parameters — so it is available where no declaration is, and it is what lets a premise chain survive a caller that omits an optional argument. A slot whose parameter has an **initializer** (the value is then the default), a **rest** parameter, a binding that is not a plain identifier, and a parameter the callee's own file **writes** are all skipped rather than stated; the list stays strictly increasing either way. Handshake protocol 32 (ADR 0048) adds the `parameter-result` derivation: the subject is the value a call to a **caller-supplied callee** handed back, and `subjectParameter` names the slot that callee was rooted at. What the caller's own function returned is the caller's, exactly as what its iterable yielded is (ADR 0042's `parameter-rooted-element`), so an accessor on it was installed by the caller and is analyzed in the caller's own artifact. Only a callee rooted as a plain `parameter` qualifies; the result of a call to a defaulted or derived one is a second hop this build does not review. Handshake protocol 31 (ADR 0047) lets an `instanceof` form carry `subjectRoot` too, for its **right** operand: the operator performs GetMethod(C, @@hasInstance) and calls it when there is one, so the whole question is whose `Symbol.hasInstance` the constructor could carry. Three answers are reviewed — `parameter`/`parameter-default`, a constructor the caller supplied, whatever it carries being the caller's; `default-library`, the engine's own constructor, whose method is `Function.prototype`'s and which carries no `subjectParameter` and no `subjectDeclaration`; and `own-class`, a class this program declares with **no heritage clause and no computed member name**, so nothing on its prototype chain can carry one, with `subjectDeclaration` naming the class. An imported constructor, a class with a superclass, a call result and a member read all state nothing. Handshake protocol 30 (ADR 0046) adds `spelling` on a `parameterPremise`: a form of the premise's type that resolves from a module which cannot name it directly, `import("<specifier>").<Name>`. A helper premise is written into a **JavaScript** module as a JSDoc `@param`, where a bare `Axis` resolves to nothing however precisely the package's declarations define it, so the premise was refused for a reason about spelling rather than about the code; the caller's twin, which does resolve the name, is where the spelling can be computed. It is a hint and never the premise — the printed `type` and the `identity` remain the whole falsifier, so a spelling that resolved to another type refuses the twin exactly as a wrong printed text does — and the established premise echoes it back byte for byte, which is why the handshake moves. A root premise carries neither identity nor spelling. Handshake protocol 29 (ADR 0045) adds `coercionPremise` on a `coercion` form and `primitiveCompletion` on every implementation transcript. A call to a module-local helper types as `any` in compiled JavaScript however well the package's declarations type the helper, so a sum of one refused wherever the premise had already typed everything else; the two fields are the missing half, in the callee's own words. `primitiveCompletion` says the checker's return type for the censused declaration — on the very program the census was classified over, the premise twin included — is a union of primitive types alone, which also settles the completion form, since a Promise and a Generator are not primitives. Because it belongs to the premise, the same helper censused under two argument premises may state it under one and not the other, and a consumer may read it only from the transcript it demanded under the premise it recorded. Handshake protocol 28 (ADR 0044) adds a third `subjectRoot` value, `own-literal`, which is not a claim about the caller: the subject is a binding this program initialized from an **object or array literal**, or from an object pattern's **rest element**, whose every own property the specification creates with CreateDataPropertyOrThrow. Reading any member of such a value — a computed key included, which is the case the checker resolves no symbol for and refuses — reaches a data property or the engine's own prototype chain. It carries `subjectDeclaration`, the exact range of the binding, and **no** `subjectParameter`; a consumer must place that declaration in the analyzed artifact's own runtime source before reading the premise. The literal must install no `get`/`set` member and no `__proto__` member, the binding must have exactly one declaration, and nothing in its file may write it. An array pattern's rest element is excluded: its elements come from the source's iterator, which is an iteration question. Handshake protocol 27 (ADR 0043) accompanies every stated `subjectParameter` with `subjectRoot`, the derivation that rooted the subject at that slot, over a closed two-value set. `parameter` is ADR 0034's premise unchanged and now covers three further spellings of the same value: the parameter itself or a read chain through it, a name an **object binding pattern in parameter position** binds when the parameter carries no default, and a name a **local variable declaration** binds from an initializer that is itself rooted, taken to a fixpoint — naming an intermediate does not change whose value it is. `parameter-default` is the new claim: the slot carries a **default** that is a reference to a parameter rooted the first way, so the value is the caller's argument at this slot or the caller's argument at the default's, caller-supplied under either branch. A rest parameter, a rest element, a binding element or parameter pattern carrying its own default, a name bound by a `for…of`/`for…in` head, and a symbol with more than one declaration are all excluded. A consumer must refuse a spelling it has not reviewed rather than read it as the weaker one, which is why the handshake moves although the field is additive. Handshake protocol 26 (ADR 0042) covers the iteration protocol. An `iteration-protocol` form may carry `subjectParameter`, the parameter its iterated value is rooted at, on a `forOfStatement`, a `spreadElement` or an array binding pattern; `implementationCall` may carry `calleeIteratedParameter`, the parameter-rooted iterable whose iteration produced the callee, stated only for a plain non-`await` `for…of` head declaring one unwritten binding; and a **rest parameter's** array is no longer recorded as an iteration form at all, because the engine constructs it, so iterating or spreading it reaches `Array.prototype` and nothing else — a syntactic fact its `any[]` type cannot supply. Handshake protocol 25 (ADR 0041) lets two further form shapes carry `subjectParameter`: an object or JSX prop **spread**, whose operand the runtime reads every own enumerable property of, and a **binding element** of an object pattern, whose subject is the value the outermost enclosing pattern destructures (a rest element included). Both are reads, so `subjectWrite` is absent for them. A protocol-24 producer roots only a property or element access, so a consumer reading a subject on these node kinds must require this protocol. Handshake protocol 24 (ADR 0040) states an uncensused accessor form's `subjectParameter` in **write** position as well as read, and adds `subjectWrite` beside it saying which position the access is in: an assignment target, a compound assignment or an update expression sets it, and a compound or update form runs the getter before the setter. A protocol-23 consumer only ever received a subject for a read, so reading the subject without the position would read a write into the caller's object as a read of it, and the handshake moves although the field is additive. `set-accessor` joins `get-accessor` and `property-access-unknown-accessor` as a kind that may carry a subject; `delete` still carries none. Handshake protocol 23 (ADR 0038, helper premises) adds optional `parameterPremises` on `exportValueDemand` — stated only beside `localDeclarationLocation`, the types the consumer asks the local declaration's form census be classified under — optional `callArgumentPremises` on `exportImplementationTranscript` — for each call of a *premised* census whose callee is a declaration in the program's own runtime source, the type each informative written argument slot carried on the twin, which is what a consumer hands back as the callee's premise — and optional `identity` on `parameterPremise`, the producer's opaque binding of a premise text to a declaration, echoed byte for byte. A local declaration's transcript may now state `parameterPremises`, equal to the demand's, when its census was classified under them; a protocol-22 consumer refused any premise on a local declaration and never asked for one, so the handshake moves. Handshake protocol 22 (ADR 0038) adds optional `parameterPremises` and `parameterPremiseRefusal` on `exportImplementationTranscript`: when present, the uncensused-form census of that implementation was classified with each parameter bound to the type the export's declared call signature gives its position — the signature a consumer compiles against and a synthesized veto samples from — rather than to the implicit `any` of an unannotated JavaScript parameter, so a coercion or iteration over a parameter declared `number` records no form. An absent list is the strictly more refusing classification over the parameters' own types and never a premise; a present one is a condition a consumer records on whatever it closes. The handshake moves because an empty form list gains a new meaning on a premised transcript. Handshake protocol 18 (ADR 0034) adds optional `subjectParameter` on `uncensusedInvokingForm` — the parameter of the transcript's own declaration at which a read accessor's receiver chain is rooted, stated only for a plain, uninitialized, non-rest parameter written nowhere in its file in a declaration mentioning neither `arguments` nor `eval` — and optional `callReceiver`/`thisParameter` on `implementationCall` for a `.call`/`.apply` whose resolved callee is the default library's Function.prototype member. An absent fact on an older producer is never a statement that the subject is unrooted, so the handshake moves. Handshake protocol 16 adds optional `returnSite.parameter`: positive identity of an unchanged whole input binding, never inferred from a missing fact or concrete return type. Protocol 15 splits control-flow incompleteness into classes and stops withholding call rows. `controlFlowCensus.incompleteness` states, per construct and at its exact location, which of two different things a `unsupported` marker means: `reachability-lower-bound`, a construct walked in full whose enclosed sites are all recorded and none called `unreachable` on its account, so only the *guarantee* is missing and a may-execute enumeration stands; or `flow-unaccounted`, a construct whose flow the census cannot account for at all, which is also the classifier's default so an unclassified marker refuses on arrival. In the same protocol the implementation call census no longer drops a call that lies in a region a `break` or `continue` makes non-universal: the row is emitted with `reach` `unknown`, the weakest non-negative value, because a dropped row is silence and silence is indistinguishable from the absence of the call. An *absent* `incompleteness` beside a nonempty `unsupported` is a producer with no classification, which a consumer must refuse, and no decoder can separate it from a present empty one — so the handshake protocol is the discriminator here too. Handshake protocol 14 added the two facts an implementation census needs: `uncensusedInvokingForms` on `exportImplementationTranscript`, one row per syntactic position that can invoke user code and that `calls` — which holds `CallExpression` and `NewExpression` only — does not record, over a closed twelve-kind vocabulary whose default is the refusing `unclassified-invoking-form`; and `localDeclarationLocation` on `exportValueDemand`, answered by `localDeclaration`, an implementation transcript for the function-like declaration at an exact source range, which is the only way to reach a declaration no export names. An *absent* `uncensusedInvokingForms` is a producer with no opinion and a present empty one is the positive claim that every walked form was a call, a construction, or provably non-invoking; no decoder can separate them, so the handshake protocol is the discriminator and the number moves rather than the fields being merely additive. Protocol 13 added `calleeSources` to the implementation call census: the traced value provenance of the callee expression, from the same tracer and under the same gates that answer `argumentSources` for an argument and `sources` for a return site, with an empty list meaning the producer traced nothing and never a negative claim about the callee. It coexists with `target`/`targetName`/`targetModule`/`declaration`/`calleeParameter`, which state the callee's *resolution* and are unchanged. Protocol 12 added `argumentSources`: per written argument slot, the traced value provenance of the expression written there, and narrowed that tracer's identifier arm to a single-declaration array binding element that is never assigned and carries neither a rest token nor a default, so a `ReturnSite.sources` a protocol-11 producer states may be withheld here. Protocol 11 split the callable-path census into declared members and apparent leaves: every path fact carries `apparent`, true for a member a value has only through the compiler's global-Function augmentation on a node with call or construct signatures. V1 is the sole active lifecycle schema. The retained table remains Wire schema v18 because invocation and exported-value transcripts are demand-shaped side answers rather than retained rows. The producer hashes this file and reports the digest in its startup handshake; both executables additionally ship in build-ID lockstep.

bytes.description: CBOR byte string; JSON Schema has no byte-string type.

moduleInventoryDemand.description: Selects how much of the resolved module graph one modules operation answers. The module inventory itself is unconditional. Imports with no importPaths covers every file the program included.

projectReferenceMapping.description: The compiler's own pairing of one input file with the declaration file emitted from it. Present only where a configured project reference covers the file, and the only declaration-to-implementation pairing TypeScript maintains. A shipped .d.ts beside a .js never has one.

moduleFact.description: One file the TypeScript program resolved and included, as the program holds it. For a module reached through a symlink the path is the realpath.

packageIdentity.description: The nearest enclosing package.json found by the compiler's own package-scope lookup, and that manifest's own name and version. An absent name or version is a fact about the manifest, not a lookup failure.

resolverPackageId.description: The package identity the resolver itself recorded while resolving one specifier. It can name a different package than the nearest enclosing manifest. subpath is the selected file's path within the package, not the exports key that led there.

moduleImportFact.description: One module specifier occurrence and what the compiler's resolver recorded for it. resolvedPath is empty exactly when resolution is unresolved. symlinkPath is populated only where the resolver's own realpath differed from the path it walked. includedPath is populated only where the program parses a different file than the one resolved, which happens for a configured project reference's declaration output and for nothing else.

compactDemands.description: Demand snapshot with one string dictionary per frame; index 0 is the empty string. Each group is [pathIndex, packedRows] where packedRows holds unsigned LEB128 (flags << 1 | hasQuery, startDelta, length) triples, each optionally followed by (queryPath, queryStart, queryLength). Bit 9 requests runtimeValueDomain, bit 10 requests callResultDomain, bit 11 requests constantValue, bit 12 requests arrayShape, bit 13 requests tupleShape, bit 14 requests libraryTypes, bit 15 requests primitiveValueDomain, bit 16 requests constructability, bit 17 requests primitiveLiteralCandidates, and bit 18 requests parameterObjectShape.

controlFlowIncompleteness.description: One construct whose flow this control-flow census does not fully model, at its exact location, classified by what is missing. `reachability-lower-bound` is a construct walked in full — every enclosed site is recorded and none is called `unreachable` on its account — whose *guarantee* alone is unmodelled, so a may-execute enumeration of the callables inside it stands. `flow-unaccounted` is a construct whose flow the census cannot account for in either direction, and it is also the classifier's default, so a marker nobody classified refuses on arrival. The class enum is closed: an unrecognized string rejects the whole transcript. Every marker in `unsupported` has at least one row here and every row's marker is in `unsupported`.

uncensusedInvokingForm.description: One syntactic position that can invoke user code and that the implementation call census does not record. The kind enum is closed: an unrecognized string rejects the whole transcript rather than degrading to an unknown row. An absent uncensusedInvokingForms array is a producer with no opinion, which a consumer must refuse; a present empty array is the positive claim that every walked form was a call, a construction, or provably non-invoking.

localLiteralResultPremise.description: Every normal completion of this exact synchronous local callee returns the same unwritten local data-only literal allocation. A terminal return covers fallthrough, and all return sites are enumerated. The consumer must bind and census the named call; an absent fact proves nothing.

initialParameterRead.description: Protocol 45: caller origin at one exact property use. An unmarked row binds an opening read; positional binds a use before every possible store; firstIterationOnly limits origin to the first loop entry. undefinedDefault binds the sole store, a body-level strict void-0 guard assigning a local empty array, and limits origin to defined caller arguments. Its use must be the first reference other than the exact guard operand and store target, and must follow the guard; at most one such row may name a parameter. These three limitations are mutually exclusive. Limited origin never proves guaranteed execution or the identity of a later use.

originalHelperRead.description: Protocol 46: one-hop possible synchronous read of an original caller input through an exact stable local helper. No guarantee, member shape, or later identity is implied.

parameterPremise.description: One parameter of the transcript's implementation bound to a type, under which uncensusedInvokingForms was classified (ADR 0038, handshake protocols 22 and 23). On an export's root implementation, type is the declared type's printed form, byte-identical to the export transcript's selectedSignature.parameters[index].value.type.text, and identity is absent. On a local declaration's transcript the entries equal the demand's exportValueDemand.parameterPremises, which the consumer copied from the caller's callArgumentPremises for the call it followed; identity is the producer's opaque binding of the text to a declaration (type flags and declaration positions), compared byte for byte and never interpreted by a consumer.

coercionPremise.description: What one `coercion` form's clearance would rest on (ADR 0045, handshake protocol 29): every operand the coercion applies ToPrimitive to is either provably a primitive by its own type — those are not listed, because a primitive has no `Symbol.toPrimitive`, `valueOf` or `toString` to reach — or the result of one of these calls into the program's own runtime source. Absent when some operand is neither, which is every shape no ADR has reviewed. Stating it is never a claim that the form clears: a consumer grants it only by matching each call to a row of the same transcript's `calls`, taking that row's own callee and premise, and requiring the callee's transcript to state `primitiveCompletion`. Four value-carrying shapes are followed to reach an operand: a conditional and the short-circuit operators (every arm must qualify), and a reference to a local binding the file declares once, writes nowhere and initializes.

callArgumentPremise.description: The type each informative written argument slot of one call carried on the twin a premised uncensused-form census ran over (handshake protocol 23). call is the location of a row of the transcript's calls, in the original file's bytes; arguments has strictly increasing indexes, and a slot it omits was `any` or unspellable. Stated only on a transcript that also states parameterPremises, and only for a call with no spread whose callee is an identifier resolving to a declaration in the program's own runtime source.

lifecycleResponse.description: Analyze carries at most one opaque tableTransition. The transition proves its base project, generation, and state token and selects full or delta mode internally. An absent transition reuses the retained table. The modules operation instead carries modules, moduleImports, and unknownImportPaths as plain rows: the resolved module graph is a property of the accepted program rather than of a demand set, so it takes no part in retained table identity.

tableTransition.description: Opaque full-or-delta Wire table transition. The active lifecycle schema emits Wire table schema v17. V15 introduced untypedCallable (tag 4), v16 added primitive literal candidates, and v17 added parameter object-construction shapes; older table schemas remain frozen and reject facts they cannot represent.

sourceArena.description: Filesystem path to a temporary file holding every source body back to back, sliced by sourceLengths. Implies a producer and client that share a filesystem.

modules.description: Every file the program included, ordered by path. A modules operation always answers it.

moduleImports.description: Resolved provenance for the requested files' module specifiers, ordered by importing path then by specifier start byte.

unknownImportPaths.description: Requested import paths the program does not hold, ordered by path. Reported rather than dropped so a caller can tell a file with no imports from a file that was never analyzed.
